name: Alif
articulation: A vertical stroke. Alif carries a long aa vowel after fatha; hamzah is a separate consonant.
mistakes: Do not treat every alif as a consonant or add a vowel without a mark.

name: Baa
articulation: Close both lips, then release for b.
mistakes: Keep its one dot below; do not confuse with taa.

name: Taa
articulation: Touch the tongue tip to the roots of the upper front teeth for a light t.
mistakes: Avoid the retroflex Hindi ट.

name: Thaa
articulation: Place the tongue tip lightly between the front teeth and let air pass, like th in thin.
mistakes: Hindi थ and Urdu س are not exact substitutes.

name: Jeem
articulation: Raise the middle of the tongue toward the hard palate for j.
mistakes: Do not replace it with z.

name: Haa (deep)
articulation: Narrow the middle throat and release a breathy, unvoiced sound without strain.
mistakes: This is distinct from ordinary ه; Hindi ह is only a cue.

name: Khaa
articulation: Raise the back of the tongue toward the soft palate and let air create friction.
mistakes: Do not replace it with aspirated ख or plain k.

name: Daal
articulation: Touch the tongue tip to the roots of the upper front teeth for d.
mistakes: Avoid retroflex ड and an extra vowel at the end.

name: Dhaal
articulation: Put the tongue tip lightly between the front teeth and voice the sound, like th in this.
mistakes: Neither z nor Hindi ध is an exact match.

name: Raa
articulation: Let the tongue tip briefly contact the upper gum ridge.
mistakes: Avoid an exaggerated repeated roll.

name: Zaay
articulation: Bring the tongue tip close to the lower front teeth and voice a z sound.
mistakes: Keep it distinct from jeem and dhaal.

name: Seen
articulation: Let air pass near the front teeth for a light s.
mistakes: Do not make it heavy like saad.

name: Sheen
articulation: Raise the middle tongue toward the hard palate for sh.
mistakes: Keep the three dots above.

name: Saad
articulation: Produce s with the back of the tongue raised, giving a full, heavy resonance.
mistakes: Plain स or seen is not equivalent; avoid adding an o vowel.

name: Daad
articulation: Bring one or both sides of the tongue against the upper molars with heavy resonance. Practise with a teacher.
mistakes: Do not substitute z, plain d, or retroflex ड.

name: Taa (heavy)
articulation: Use the tongue tip at the upper front tooth roots with the back of the tongue raised.
mistakes: Hindi ट is not an exact substitute.

name: Dhaa (heavy)
articulation: Use the tongue tip at the front tooth edges for a voiced interdental sound, with heavy resonance.
mistakes: Plain z or dhaal loses the heavy quality.

name: Ayn
articulation: Constrict the middle throat gently while voicing. Learn this unfamiliar sound directly from a teacher.
mistakes: A vowel or hamzah alone does not reproduce ayn; never strain.

name: Ghayn
articulation: Raise the back of the tongue toward the soft palate and voice a friction sound.
mistakes: Plain g is not equivalent.

name: Faa
articulation: Touch the inner lower lip to the upper front tooth edges and let air pass.
mistakes: Do not replace f with aspirated ph.

name: Qaaf
articulation: Use the deepest back of the tongue against the upper palate near the uvula.
mistakes: Keep it deeper than kaaf; plain क is only an approximation.

name: Kaaf
articulation: Use the back of the tongue slightly forward of qaaf for a light k.
mistakes: Do not make it heavy like qaaf; its small inner mark is not a dot.

name: Laam
articulation: Touch the tongue edges and tip to the upper gum area for l.
mistakes: Usually light; special Quranic cases require guided teaching.

name: Meem
articulation: Close both lips for m, allowing nasal resonance.
mistakes: Do not add an extra vowel or prolong without a rule.

name: Noon
articulation: Touch the tongue tip to the upper gums for n with nasal resonance.
mistakes: Do not confuse its one dot above with baa below.

name: Haa (light)
articulation: Release a gentle h from the deepest throat, with relaxed airflow.
mistakes: Keep it distinct from the middle-throat ح.

name: Waaw
articulation: Round both lips for w without touching the upper teeth; it can also carry long oo.
mistakes: Hindi व may involve the teeth; avoid v here.

name: Yaa
articulation: Raise the middle tongue for y; it can also carry long ee.
mistakes: Keep its two dots below in the isolated form.
